"It was a pure and simple remark by an old shopkeeper during his extempore speech under the peculiar facts and circumstances and had stated certain objectionable words at the moment, without carrying requisite intention to humiliate the Deputy Commissioner or any other member of the Schedule Caste," the Court said. The Court said at the worst it could be said that he had questioned the "intelligence/competence" of the Deputy Commissioner. "He had simply stated that by taking advantage of reservation in Government jobs, the Deputy Commissioner was selected by the U.P.S.C and due to her Harijan Caste, she was deputed as a Deputy Commissioner," the Court added. The SC/ST Act provisions deal with intentional insult or intimidation of a member of a scheduled caste or scheduled tribe in public view and promoting enmity, hatred or ill-will against members of these communities, respectively. items.title: No relief for Tata Trusts as Bombay High Court refuses to halt Tata Sons' November 30 board meeting
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Friday refused to stay the crucial board meeting of Tata Sons scheduled for November 30, even as Tata Trusts pushed for a stay on the same. Justice Abhay Ahuja said, "We are giving you time to file reply. I am not granting any relief. Let meeting go on November 30 and the meeting is subject to the outcome of the petition." Justice Abhay Ahuja The matter will be heard next on January 21, 2027. Tata Trusts holds a 66% stake in Tata Sons. It has challenged a September 17 board resolution that reappoints N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for five years starting February 21, 2027. The board passed the resolution 4:1. Acting chair Harish Manwani cast a tie-breaking vote after Chandrasekaran abstained. Among the two Tata Trusts nominee directors, Venu Srinivasan voted for the move and Noel Tata voted against it. Tata Trusts argues the resolution is in violation of Articles 104B and 121 of Tata Sons’ Articles of Association. These rules require approval from a majority of trust-appointed directors on major decisions. The Trusts cite Supreme Court precedent from the Cyrus Mistry case and a legal opinion from former Chief Justice DY Chandrachud. They state a chair’s casting vote cannot override trust director rules or settle a split between trust nominees. The petitions seek court orders blocking the resolution before the November 30 board meeting. They also seek ₹65 crore in damages: ₹50 crore for Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and ₹15 crore for Ratan Tata's trust. A Charity Commissioner order has stalled joint trust representation for the annual general meeting, adding to the dispute. Appearing for the Trusts, Senior Advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi sought injunction or deferment of the board meeting scheduled for November 30. "To protect their interests of 66% there were two clauses. At least so long as shareholding does not fall below 40% there will be 1/3rd directors of trust on board. This has been the position for decades," he said. Singhvi went on to argue, "The directors were 6. 1/3rd of 6 is 2. Two directors were nominated by the Trust. One is Noel Tata and the other was Venu Srinivasan. Section 121 with 104B (of Articles of Association) says that no decision which requires voting can be taken unless there is majority of nominee trust. The competition is being organised by the Centre for International Corporate and Commercial Laws (CICCL) at MNLUCS. items.title: Jammu and Kashmir finally gets Advocate General after two-year wait
items.summary: Senior Advocate Syed Faisal Qadri has been appointed the new Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir. The post has remained vacant for two years. The last Advocate General, DC Raina, resigned from the post on October 18, 2024, following the formation of the Omar Abdullah-led government in Jammu and Kashmir. The long-pending vacancy had recently come under the Jammu and Kashmir High Court's scrutiny. A Public Interest Litigation (PIL) petition filed by advocate Harsh Dubey flagged concerns that the prolonged vacancy was affecting the administration of justice and statutory functions attached to the Advocate General's office. The plea also highlighted the impact on the Jammu and Kashmir Advocates’ Welfare Fund Trustee Committee, of which the Advocate General is the ex-officio chairperson. On November 5, the Jammu and Kashmir administration assured the High Court that the appointment process was underway and that the post would be filled within one month. Qadri's appointment as the new Advocate General was notified today. [Read Notification]

items.title: Lionel Messi event row: Kerala High Court refuses to stay criminal case against Reporter TV MD Anto Augustine
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Friday refused to stay criminal proceedings against Reporter TV MD Anto Augustine in a case tied to allegations of cheating and criminal conspiracy over a failed attempt to bring the Argentinian national team and footballer Lionel Messi to Kerala. Justice PV Balakrishnan was hearing Augustine's plea to quash the case. Augustine's counsel today highlighted that the investigating authorities had earlier indicated that they had no intention to arrest him and that this assurance had prompted the closure of an anticipatory bail plea. Despite this, Augustine was now being harassed with notices from the investigation team, the counsel claimed. "When the (anticipatory) bail application was heard, they specifically stated that they have no intention to arrest but they are unnecessarily sending notices." The Court, however, was not inclined to grant Augustine any interim relief today, and confined to granting the State time to respond to the Reporter TV MD's petition. "When the DG of Prosecution is asking for time it is only proper to allow it," the judge said. The matter will be heard next after ten days. Justice PV Balakrishnan The first information report (FIR) in the case was registered by the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing alleged financial irregularities connected with the failed event for which Augustine's Reporter Broadcasting Company (RBC) was the main commercial sponsor. The FIR alleges that Augustine had conspired to add illegal and fake details in an agreement signed with the Argentina Football Association to cheat the State government. It also alleged that Augustine had conspired to secure an exemption from paying a ₹5-crore security deposit to occupy the Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium in Kochi. Augustine moved the present petition before the Kerala High Court to quash this FIR and all consequent criminal proceedings against him. In September this year, the SIT carried out searches at several locations linked to Augustine as part of its probe into the failed Messi event. During one such raid at his family home in Wayanad, authorities recovered roughly 67 litres of foreign liquor and wine, which exceeds the legally permissible limit for personal possession. A separate criminal case was registered by the Excise Department in which Augustine was arrested. However, he was granted bail in that case by the High Court on September 22.

items.title: Calcutta High Court sets aside appointment of Ritabrata Banerjee as West Bengal Leader of Opposition, orders fresh decision
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Friday set aside the West Bengal Legislative Assembly Speaker's decision to appoint Ritabrata Banerjee as Leader of Opposition, and ordered a fresh decision in the matter. The Court has directed the Speaker to reconsider the issue of who should be the Leader of Opposition (LoP) in West Bengal within ten days. Justice Krishna Rao also set aside the appointment of Akhruzzaman as the Chief Whip for the opposition party, namely the Trinamool Congress Party (TMC). Justice Krishna Rao The Court passed the ruling on a petition by TMC (Mamata Banerjee faction) leader Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay, challenging the Speaker's appointment of the rival TMC (Democratic Trinamool Congress) faction leader Ritabrata Banerjee as the Leader of Opposition in the West Bengal Legislative Assembly. The dispute stems majorly from the Speaker's decision to set aside what was AITC (Mamata) claimed was a settled decision to nominate Chattopadhyay as the LoP. Instead the Speaker named Ritabrata Banerjee, who has since broken away from the Trinamool Congress (presently Mamata-All India Trinamool Congress) to form his own rebel faction known as Democratic Trinamool Congress. According to the plea, subsequent to the BJP's win in the Legislative Assembly Elections, a meeting was held at the AITC party headquarters on May 6, 2026 where Chattopadhyay's nomination as the Leader of Opposition was confirmed. Approximately 70 AITC leaders, including Banerjee were in attendance. Subsequently, a signed resolution by then AITC members dated May 19, 2026, confirming Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay's nomination as the Leader of Opposition, was communicated to the Speaker. An attendance sheet of the members attending the May 6 meeting was also conveyed. At this stage, however, Banerjee made a complaint to the Speaker alleging that many of the signatures in the resolution were forged. According to the plea, the Speaker then went on to direct the registration of a police complaint against then-AITC General Secretary Abhishek Banerjee for allegedly falsifying the signatures on the resolution. items.title: Supreme Court slams TN for not lighting lamp at Thiruparankundram; suspends temple trustees, orders lighting of lamp on Nov 28
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday took strong exception to the State of Tamil Nadu and Madurai district officials for failing to comply with the November 20 order of the top court to light Karthigai Deepam at the disputed stone pillar (Deepathoon) on Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai. A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi suspended the current board of trustees of the Subramaniya Swami Temple for defying the Court's directions. It then proceeded to appoint retired Justices S Vaidyanathan and V Parthiban as receivers of the trust of the temple and directed that the Karthigai Deepam be lit at the Deepathoon tomorrow, November 28. The Court directed the court-appointed receivers, entrusted with the administration of the temple after the supersession of its board of trustees, to ensure the lighting of the lamp. The security of the temple perimeter was directed to be handed over to the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF). In departure from its November 20 order, the Court said that every devotee can light the lamp at the disputed site at least 50 metres away from the nearby Dargah on all sides. The earlier order had permitted lighting of the lamp only by a small team. The CRPF was also ordered to protect the nearby Dargah and ensure that Muslim devotees visiting it are neither obstructed nor prevented from offering prayers. Pertinently, the bench ordered the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary to file a comprehensive affidavit detailing emails, telephone calls and messages exchanged between officials with regard to the issue surrounding the lighting of the lamp and the Court's November 20 order. "The chain of events that has unfolded in the instant case would indicate that the executive authorities seem to have acted at the dictates of their political bosses," the Supreme Court said. The bench also ordered the Chief Secretary of Tamil Nadu to remain personally present before it on the next date of hearing. Further, the Court issued contempt of court notices to the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, Director General of Police, Hindu Religious & Charitable Endowments Secretary and Commissioner, Madurai District Collector, Commissioner of Police, Superintendent of Police, temple authorities and others. The Court expressed pain and anguish at the developments over the November 20 order and said that non-compliance with its order reflected administrative chaos in the administration in the State of Tamil Nadu or at least in Madurai district. items.title: Community with 5% population has 40% representation in Supreme Court: Former CJI BR Gavai writes to President of India
items.summary: Former Chief Justice of India (CJI) BR Gavai has written to President of India Droupadi Murmu raising concerns that recent recommendations by the Supreme Court Collegium for the appointment or transfer of judges favour one particular community at the cost of merit, diversity and inclusivity. In a three-page letter dated November 27, Gavai questioned the functioning of the Collegium and said that recent developments warranted immediate remedial measures by all stakeholders. “Candidates belonging to one particular section of the society are being favoured for recommendation/elevation to the exclusion of everyone else including marginalized communities," the letter said. Gavai said that a particular community (left unnamed in the letter) that constitutes less than 5 per cent of the country's population has had over 40 per cent representation in the Supreme Court, and that their representation has risen manifold in the recent past. "I admit that this is not something new and that is precisely why it is increasingly becoming unforgivable," Justice Gavai expressed. His letter adds that apart from such appointments resulting in the exclusion of candidates from marginalised backgrounds (scheduled castes, scheduled tribes, other backward classes, minorities, and women) even members of forward communities are being left out if they do not belong to the "particular" community. "I may not be misunderstood as being opposed to any section of the society in so far as the candidates belonging to forward section are duly considered and my endeavor has always been to strike balance between all the sections. However, now there (are) compelling circumstances which support the perception that increasingly recommendations are being made with a focus on appeasing and rewarding a single community," he further said. items.title: Madras High Court refuses to reject election petition against CM Vijay’s Perambur win
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Friday dismissed Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s application to reject an election petition challenging his victory from the Perambur Assembly constituency. Justice V Lakshminarayanan held that the petition filed by S Dinesh, a voter from Perambur, disclosed a cause of action and is maintainable. The judge said the alleged omissions and discrepancies in Vijay’s nomination affidavit had been specifically pleaded and that their significance could only be assessed at trial. Justice V Lakshminarayanan The order was passed after Vijay filed an application seeking rejection of the election petition filed by S Dinesh, a voter in the constituency, who alleged that the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) chief had withheld or misstated details of several property transactions in the affidavit he filed with his nomination papers. Dinesh asked the Madras High Court to set aside Vijay’s election. Dinesh alleged that Vijay had failed to disclose the purchase of three acres in Panruti for ₹30 crore in January 2026 and the sale of a commercial property in Padi for ₹35 crore the following month. He also claimed that a 50-cent parcel in Kodaikanal that Vijay had declared as agricultural land was classified as government land in revenue records Dinesh argued that the alleged omissions deprived voters of information they were entitled to and amounted to undue influence, a corrupt practice under Section 123(2) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951. Vijay denied the allegations and sought rejection of the petition at the threshold, arguing that it did not set out the material facts needed to make out a case. His lawyers submitted that Vijay had declared assets worth more than ₹600 crore and that the alleged discrepancies did not show how voters’ choices had been influenced. Vijay secured 1,20,365 votes in Perambur in the April 2026 Assembly election, defeating the DMK’s RD Shekar by 53,715 votes. He also won from Tiruchirappalli East, which he vacated to retain Perambur. Shekar and another Perambur voter, TN Lakshmi Narasimhan, filed separate petitions challenging the Perambur result. items.title: Supreme Court cautions lawyers against responding "belligerently" to questions asked by judges
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday said that lawyers should not assume that every question put by a judge is an adversarial stance against their client, and should refrain from responding belligerently to such queries by the court [ P Kathirvel vs. State ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran recorded its disapproval of the conduct of a Senior Advocate appearing in a case. The Bench noted that he took umbrage at the Court's queries and repeatedly accused the judges of not hearing him. "We mention this only to caution the minority in the bar, who takes every syllable uttered by a judge to be a stance taken against the client he represents in court and respond acrimoniously to the bench." it noted . The Bench stressed that counsel must assist the court in a non-acrimonious manner rather than placing judges in an adversarial position. "It would be always in the fitness of things to carry on the assistance in a non- acrimonious mood, which the majority of the Bar realise, and do not place the courts in an adversarial role. The majority of the learned counsel appearing in courts, quite aware of their relevance as a major stake holder in the justice delivery system, often term their submissions as ‘assistance’ to the court. Rightly so; without which the courts will be at sea, with the voluminous records and the long list of cases on the board, on any given day," it said. Despite the courtroom exchange, the bench examined the record on its own and quashed criminal proceedings initiated by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) against two customs officers - Assistant Commissioner P Kathirvel and Examiner S Gugan - in a 2012 corruption case. In doing so, the Court noted that an aggrieved litigant should not be made to suffer because of counsel's conduct. "As we would presently see, if the proceedings were carried on amicably the Senior Counsel could have assisted us better, as the records, contain the answer to our queries; which we perused minutely, since despite the acrimonious repartees we realise that there is an aggrieved litigant behind, who shall not suffer," the Court remarked. items.title: Two judges resigned after intervention by Chief Justice of India during my tenure: Justice SK Kaul
items.summary: Former Supreme Court Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul on Wednesday recalled two instances during his tenure when judges were asked to resign after the intervention of Chief Justice of India. He said the moral authority of the then Chief Justices of India prompted the judges to resign rather than go through a formal process. “ There have been cases where, during my tenure, a judge has been called, asked to put in his papers and has put in his papers. There are two cases I clearly remember where this has happened. And so, the moral authority of the Chief Justices of India in both cases made the judge resign rather than go through any process, ” Justice Kaul recalled. Justice Kaul was speaking during a fireside chat with Senior Advocate Saurabh Kirpal at the launch of his book, Without Fear or Favour. The event took place at the India International Centre (IIC) in New Delhi. The book was unveiled by Supreme Court Justice Vikram Nath and former Supreme Court Justice V Ramasubramanian . Justice SK Kaul book launch Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul There have been cases where, during my tenure, a judge has been called, asked to put in his papers and has put in his papers. The conversation also touched on the role of politics and personal preferences in judicial appointments. Justice Kaul pointed to instances where people, overlooked under one political dispensation, were appointed after a change in government. “ There have been judges who didn’t make it till a particular stage of time with a particular dispensation. The moment the dispensation changes, the person becomes a judge. Suddenly, he doesn’t acquire some great abilities. And this has been happening over a period of time,’ the former top court judge added. Kirpal asked whether judges in the Collegium had always managed to keep personal likes and dislikes out of appointment decisions. “ We are all human beings. It’s not possible ,” Justice Kaul replied. items.title: Are those who turned innocent people into Naxals behind bars? President Droupadi Murmu asks
items.summary: President Droupadi Murmu on Thursday said those surrendering as Naxals had been brainwashed and drawn into the movement, and called for efforts to understand why innocent people were made to become Naxals. Speaking at the Constitution Day celebrations at the Supreme Court of India, Murmu said the country has become Naxal-free and that those who had surrendered should be treated with compassion. "मैं धन्यवाद देना चाहती हूँ सरकार को। आज पूरा देश नक्सल मुक्त हो गया है। जो नक्सल सरेंडर कर रहे थे, मैं उनके चेहरे देख रही थी। उनका मासूम चेहरा देखकर मुझे नहीं लगता कि ये नक्सल हैं। इन्हें नक्सल बनाया गया है। पता नहीं, जिन लोगों ने इन्हें बनाया है, वे अंदर हैं कि नहीं। लेकिन जिन लोगों को जबरदस्ती नक्सल बनाया गया है, वे लोग अंदर हैं। उसके ऊपर थोड़ा काम करना चाहिए, क्योंकि वे लोग मासूम हैं।" said Murmu. [Translation] "I would like to thank the government. Today, the entire country has become free of Naxalism. I was watching the faces of those who were surrendering. Looking at their innocent faces, I do not feel that they are Naxals. They have been made into Naxals. I do not know whether the people who made them Naxals are inside [jail] or not. But the people who were forcibly made into Naxals are inside [jail]. Some work should be done on that as well, because they are innocent people," said Murmu. She further observed that efforts must be made to understand why some people were drawn into Naxalism and called for society to take responsibility for their welfare. items.title: Revised petrol pump plan requires fresh NOC from ADM; PESO approval not enough: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently held that a revised plan for establishing a petrol pump requires fresh clearance from the Additional District Magistrate (ADM) even if the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO) has approved it. [Naseef Meethale Paingol v Sreekandhan R & ors and connected cases] A bench of Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji made the observation while considering appeals filed by Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and a petrol pump dealer against a single judge's direction to reconsider clearance for a proposed fuel outlet near a school in Kannur. In its judgment dated November 12, the Court clarified that granting a No Objection Certificate (NOC) for a petrol pump under Rule 144 of the Petroleum Rules 2002 (Rules) is not just a procedural formality, as the district authority who is in charge of that area needs to carefully examine various safety concerns before granting clearance. " As correctly asserted by Sri.Santhosh Mathew, the 'NOC' issued by an 'ADM' is not a formality; or the culmination of a mechanical process; it surely cannot be allowed to be so either. There is a serious and important purpose behind Rule 144 of the 'Rules' because it is the District Authority — who is in charge of the area in question — who can understand and incisively assess ground realities, as also its necessities and requirements, " the Court said. Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji The dispute arose after BPCL issued a letter of intent to dealer, Naseef Meethale Paingol, to establish a petrol pump in Kannur. Although the proposed site plan received PESO approval, the Additional District Magistrate (ADM) initially refused to issue the necessary NOC. However, on October 6, 2025, after a modified plan was submitted, the dealer secured an NOC from the ADM. Subsequently, the manager of a nearby school and two local residents challenged the NOC before a single-judge raising concerns about safety and compliance with mandatory distance requirements. The dealer then prepared a third site plan, shifting the location of the fuel dispensing unit to comply with the applicable distance rules, which was also approved by the PESO on March 2, 2026. Considering this development, the Court directed the ADM to reconsider the NOC based on the latest plan. The dealer and BPCL challenged this direction of the single-judge before the Division Bench. items.title: What Tata Trusts’ suits in Bombay High Court say against N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment
items.summary: Trustees of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) have filed a suit before the Bombay High Court challenging a board resolution passed by Tata Sons Private Limited on September 17. That resolution has sought to reappoint Natarajan Chandrasekaran as the Executive Chairman of Tata Sons for another five years. The resolution was passed 4:1. Directors Venu Srinivasan, Harish Manwani, Anita M George and Saurabh Agrawal voted in favour. Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata voted against it while Chandrasekaran abstained. Tata Trusts, which controls 66% stake in Tata Sons, has argued that the reappointment resolution is void ab initio. They have sought a declaration that the resolution is ultra vires the Articles of Association and, hence, null and void. It has sought an order to restrain the company from acting on the reappointment. SDTT has also sought a bar on the board chair casting vote when 2 trust nominees disagree. Relief has been sought ahead of the November 30 board meeting. The trusts have collectively sought damages to the tune of ₹65 crore: ₹50 crore by SDTT, and ₹15 crore by RDTT. Here is a summary of the suits filed before the High Court. Named defendants The suit names the following defendants: Tata Sons; Natarajan Chandrasekaran; Saurabh Agrawal; Harish Manwani; Anita George; Venu Srinivasan; and Noel N Tata (no reliefs sought against him) Board meeting under scrutiny Chandrasekaran e-mailed the board on August 12, 2026, stating he would not seek reappointment when his term ends on February 20, 2027. SDTT and five other trusts passed resolutions on August 13 respecting that decision and asked the company to help constitute a selection committee under Article 118. At the September 17 meeting, Chandrasekaran said he had reconsidered and was willing to be appointed for another five-year term from February 21, 2027 to February 20, 2032. Two Trust directors nominated under Article 104B of the Articles of Association of Tata Sons were present: Srinivasan voted in favour, while Noel Tata objected and voted against it. Chandrasekaran recused himself as an interested director. Acting chair for the agenda, Harish Manwani, exercised a casting vote to treat the resolution as passed. Core of the dispute: Article 121 of the Articles of Association Article 121 requires “the affirmative vote of a majority of the (Trust) Directors appointed pursuant to Article 104B present at the meeting" on matters decided by a majority of directors. items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday criticised the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) for not disclosing, even to the court, the “security inputs” which formed the basis for cancellation of the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) registration of NGO Socio-Legal Information Centre (SLIC). SLIC is a non-governmental organisation (NGO) that describes itself as a legal aid and education organisation. In his order, Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani noted that the NGO faced drastic action because of these security inputs, adding that they cannot be kept secret to the point that no material is shown even to the Court. “While the respondent [government] contends that the violations on the appellant’s [NGO’s] part were brought to its notice through ‘security inputs’, which cannot be divulged since they are ‘secret’; this court is of the view that such inputs cannot be kept secret to the point that no material is brought even to the notice of this court, though the appellant has faced the drastic action of having its FCRA registration cancelled, arising from such inputs,” the Court said. The Court quashed the government’s order cancelling the NGO’s FCRA registration and pulled up the authorities for stating that the NGO portrayed “wrong image of public institutions of India in the eyes of international community.” Justice Bhambhani said that such an allegation strains credulity and the Court is dismayed by the government’s "attempt to baselessly portray the appellant organisation in such light” . “This court is further of the view that the impugned cancellation order is misconceived, untenable and illegal, apart from being disproportionate and excessive in its rigour and impact,” the Court concluded. It added that Section 14(2) of the FCRA requires a personal hearing before cancellation of registration, and that merely issuing a show-cause notice is insufficient given the serious consequences. items.title: Saket court acquits former My FM CEO of sexual harassment charges
items.summary: A Delhi court on Monday acquitted Harish M Bhatia, former CEO of My FM, the radio arm of the Dainik Bhaskar Group, of the charges of outraging and insulting the modesty of a woman. Judicial Magistrate First Class Shivangi Vyas of Saket courts held that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. The Court reiterated that a conviction in a sexual offence can be based solely n a complainant's testimony only if the same is of sterling quality. "The conviction in a sexual offence case can be based solely on the testimony of prosecutrix provided her testimony is of sterling quality that is wholly reliable, consistent and inspires confidence," it said. Where the case rests primarily on that testimony, the Court must scrutinize it with greater care to ensure that it is free from material contradictions, improvements, omissions or inherent improbabilities, the judge added. Since the same was not satisfied in the present case, Bhatia was acquitted of all charges. The complainant, then National Programming Head, alleged harassment between 2008 and 2010 at the workplace, office parties and tours. Her final allegation concerned May 7, 2010, when Bhatia allegedly called her to his cabin, held her hands and demanded sexual favours. He was booked for offences under Sections 354 (assault with intent to outrage modesty) and 509 (word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). The Court found three conflicting versions about her resignation. In her complaint she said it was forced, in her testimony she denied sending any resignation, and in her first complaint to the National Commission for Women she said she resigned on grounds of ill health. The Court held that they were all contradictory to each other. It also noted that the allegations in her testimony were far graver than those in her complaint. "It is not a case of minor omissions in the complaint and explanation of the alleged act in detail in the testimony of complainant during trial rather it is a case of major omission in her complaint and material improvements in her testimony during trial," the Court said. On an alleged incident at hotel dinner party in November 2008, the Court noted that the complainant was the only public witness to the same. items.summary: Members of the Knanaya Catholic community have moved the Supreme Court challenging a March 23 Kerala High Court judgment that refused to recognise the community as a separate religious denomination and invalidated its centuries-old rule of endogamy [ Jose Mathew & Anr v. The Metropolitan Archbishop & Ors. ]. When the appeal - alongside connected appeals - came up for hearing on Wednesday, a Bench of Justices BV Nagarathna , R Mahadevan , and Sanjeev Sachdeva adjourned the matter to the first week of January without issuing notice on the plea. The Court observed that the nine-judge Constitution Bench verdict in the Sabarimala reference case is expected to be pronounced before the Court closes for winter vacations on December 18 and may have a substantial bearing on the present case. items.title: Madras High Court calls Murugappa Group sisters feud over ₹1,750 crore fortune "ego fight", urges settlement
items.summary: The Madras High Court has directed Valli Arunachalam, daughter of former Murugappa Group chairman MV Murugappan, and her family members to deposit ₹974.94 crore before the Court in a dispute with her younger sister Vellachi Murugappan over the partition of family assets worth nearly ₹1,750 crore. A Bench of Justices N Sathish Kumar and GK Muthukumaar described the litigation as an apparent ego fight between the sisters and urged them to settle their differences amicably. “ Since the entire issue appears to be only an ego fight between the sisters, viz., the 1st plaintiff and the 2nd respondent, we are of the view that the matter can be given a quietus, if the parties are really interested in resolving the dispute by arriving at an amicable settlement ,” the Court observed. Arunachalam, a nuclear scientist, had previously made headlines for her legal battle against the larger business family over representation on the board of Ambadi Investments Limited, the group's holding company. The sisters were on the same side in that dispute, which culminated in a family settlement in August 2023. Founded in 1900, the Murugappa Group is a ₹1.05 lakh crore business conglomerate with interests in financial services, agriculture and engineering. Its ten listed companies include Cholamandalam Investment and Finance, CG Power, Coromandel International and Tube Investments of India. The present dispute concerns assets held by the MV Murugappan Hindu Undivided Family (HUF), constituted in 1957. Following their father's death, Arunachalam assumed office as the karta of the HUF with Vellachi's consent. However, differences subsequently arose over the administration and partition of the family assets. Vellachi and her two children instituted a partition suit in 2025, claiming half of the HUF assets. She alleged that Arunachalam had failed to furnish complete financial records despite repeated requests. She also objected to a draft partition deed of June 2024, which contemplated payment of approximately ₹100 crore to Arunachalam in recognition of her contribution towards augmenting the family wealth. Arunachalam maintained that she had substantially enhanced the value of the assets through prudent investments and that the proposal was never acted upon. items.title: Small mercies and large silences: The Supreme Court and the Constitution at 77
items.summary: Every November 26, the Supreme Court’s lawns are scrubbed, the ceremonial speeches are dusted off and the Republic congratulates itself on the durability of its founding charter. Constitution Day invites easy theatrics. Critics declare the document dead on arrival; loyalists hail the bench as an infallible shield against executive excess. The Supreme Court’s record across 2026 resists both caricatures. Over the past 11 months, the Court has displayed a striking split personality. When confronting the daily, retail indignities inflicted on ordinary citizens by municipal apathy, police high-handedness or bureaucratic drift, the Court has been remarkably imaginative. Yet, when asked to scrutinise the institutional architecture of democracy itself, the same Court has repeatedly blinked, deferred or stalled in the vestibule. The guardian of the sidewalk Take the Court’s record on individual dignity and personal liberty this year and there is genuine constitutional craftsmanship to admire. In June, while hearing a petition on road safety, a bench elevated something Indians routinely treat as an urban luxury into an enforceable right. It held that walking safely on unobstructed, demarcated footpaths flows directly from Article 19(1)(d) and Article 21, imposing binding obligations on civic authorities. For citizens forced onto speeding carriageways because municipalities surrender pavements to encroachments, reading that basic mobility into the Constitution was no trivial gesture. That instinct to police everyday abuses carried steadily through the autumn docket. Earlier this month, in Sri Sujit Das , the Court closed a favorite loophole of investigative agencies. It ruled that the constitutional 24-hour clock under Article 22(2) for producing a detainee before a magistrate begins ticking from the moment liberty is actually curtailed , not whenever an officer records a formal arrest. Days later, in Devilal Gond , it ordered compensation for a man kept languishing behind bars for over seven years after his High Court acquittal because administrative paperwork moved slower than human despair. Nor did the Court shy away from hard moral and ecological questions affecting vulnerable communities. items.title: Delhi High Court restrains Old Monk maker from selling its iQ gin in packaging resembling Greater Than
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday restrained Mohan Meakin Limited from manufacturing and selling its iQ gin in packaging that is deceptively similar to the overall get-up of Nao Spirits and Beverages Private Limited’s Greater Than gin [Nao Spirits and Beverages Private Limited v Mohan Meakin Limited] Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav passed the order in a suit filed by Nao Spirits, which accused Mohan Meakin of copying the overall packaging of its flagship product, Greater Than London Dry Gin, launched in India in 2016. Mohan Meakin, which has been in the liquor business for over 160 years, markets brands including Old Monk, Big Ben London gin and Jamun gin. It launched iQ gin in August 2023. In an interim order, the Court said that Nao Spirits had established a strong prima facie case of passing off. It found that the rival products shared several prominent features, including practically the same bottle silhouette, a tall black cap, a predominantly black-and-white colour scheme and a large angular device placed at the top centre of the label. “The broad similarities between the two bottles are obvious at the first look, and the differences are nudged into oblivion,” the Court observed. However, the Court added that the use of the get-up was likely to cause confusion and deception among ordinary consumers. Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav Mohan Meakin had earlier argued that the bottle was an ordinary, generic and functional design and that black and white colours could not be monopolised by Nao Spirits. It also pointed to differences in the labels, brand names, bottle dimensions and closures. However, in the order pronounced today, the Court noted that consumers often encounter liquor bottles from a distance, behind counters or on bar shelves. It observed that a consumer could believe that iQ gin was another product made by the makers of Greater Than, or one manufactured with their approval. Thus, the Court restrained Mohan Meakin from manufacturing or bottling any fresh stock of gin in the same get-up. It granted the company 30 days to exhaust the existing stock. Rival products The Court clarified that Mohan Meakin is not restrained from using the iQ mark or its device. It also said that Nao Spirits has no monopoly over black and white colours. However, any new packaging must differ in the bottle shape, label size and placement, colour arrangement, device placement and typography, the Court said. items.title: Allahabad High Court verdict denying right to wear hijab in school not a precedent: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently said that the Allahabad High Court's August 21 judgment upholding a school's ban on wearing a hijab in classrooms shall not be treated as a precedent [ Muslim Womens Study Circle vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi made the observation while issuing notice to the State of Uttar Pradesh on a an appeal challenging the High Court verdict. The Court tagged the matter with the pending batch of appeals arising out of the Karnataka hijab ban case . "Permission to file the petition is granted. Issue notice. Tag with Civil Appeal No. 7095/2022 and this judgment shall not be treated as precedent," the Bench recorded in its November 20 order. Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi The appeal before the apex court was filed against the High Court's August 21 judgment, which had upheld a school's classroom ban on headscarves while ruling that wearing a hijab is not an essential religious practice in Islam. In that ruling, a Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court comprising Justices JJ Munir and Indrajeet Shukla dismissed a petition filed by a Muslim student, Sukaina Rizvi, seeking directions to allow her to wear a headscarf along with the prescribed uniform at Tagore Public School in Prayagraj's Attarsuiya. The petitioner submitted that she had worn a headscarf since joining the school in class VI but was denied admission to class XI on the ground that wearing a hijab violated the school's dress code. Rejecting her plea, the High Court held that no authoritative religious text or material had been placed on record to establish that wearing a headscarf inside a classroom is an essential religious practice under Article 25 of the Constitution. It also noted that the Karnataka High Court's Full Bench verdict upholding restrictions on hijabs in educational institutions continued to hold persuasive value in the absence of a final authoritative pronouncement by the Supreme Court following its 2022 split verdict. The High Court further ruled that the school's past inaction or tolerance in lower classes did not create an estoppel against enforcing a uniform dress code in higher classes. A uniform policy promotes discipline, equality, and a religion-neutral atmosphere, the Court added. Challenging this verdict, the Muslim Women's Study Circle moved the Supreme Court. items.title: 10 former CJIs inaugurate India's first Chief Justices of India Museum at OP Jindal Global University
items.summary: On the eve of Constitution Day, 10 former Chief Justices of India came together, in person or virtually, to inaugurate India’s first Chief Justices of India Museum at OP Jindal Global University (JGU). Envisioned as “Guardians of the Republic,” the Museum brings judicial history into conversation with art, technology and personal testimony, inviting visitors to explore how justice shapes individual lives and the destiny of a nation. Across five galleries, it features more than 280 busts of Supreme Court judges, models of 25 High Courts, 22 language tapestries, 20 interactive biographical pillars and 20 defining judgments, alongside a holographic courtroom and an extensive collection of artworks, sculptures and installations. The inauguration brought together former Chief Justices MN Venkatachaliah , BN Kirpal , S Rajendra Babu , KG Balakrishnan , P Sathasivam , RM Lodha , Dipak Misra , SA Bobde , UU Lalit and BR Gavai . Hailing the occasion, Naveen Jindal , the Founding Chancellor of JGU said, “The Constitution of India is the enduring foundation of our Republic, embodying the ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. India’s first museum dedicated to the Chief Justices extends the vision of our Constitution Museum by honouring the Supreme Court’s guardianship of these constitutional values. My own journey to secure every citizen’s right to fly the national flag taught me that the Constitution is not a distant text but a living promise, kept alive by an independent judiciary that listens to the citizen. The Supreme Court’s recognition of that right in 2004 remains, for me, a lasting reminder of what our courts mean for the freedom of ordinary Indians.” Articulating the vision behind the Museum, Prof (Dr) C Raj Kumar , the Founding Vice Chancellor of JGU said, “The Chief Justices of India Museum explores justice as an evolving idea, tracing how the Supreme Court of India, through its Chief Justices and Judges, has shaped the nation’s constitutional democracy. It presents the Office of the Chief Justice as a living institution that has interpreted, protected and strengthened the Constitution through moments of national transformation. items.title: Builder-bank nexus: Supreme Court directs HDFC, ICICI Bank chiefs to grant prosecution sanctions or appear before court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday directed HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital and PNB Housing Finance to grant unconditional sanction to prosecute their officials within one week in connection with an alleged builder-financier nexus that has left several homebuyers in financial distress [Himanshu Singh vs Union of India] A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana warned that the heads of these financial institutions would have to personally appear before the Court in case of non-compliance. The Court was hearing a batch of petitions concerning subvention schemes under which homebuyers were subjected to loan recovery proceedings despite builders' failure to honour their financial commitments. “We direct all the banks or financial institutions referred to above to issue unconditional sanction for prosecution within one week, failing which the CMD and Chairman shall remain present in Court to show cause as to why appropriate action be not taken against them,” the Court ordered. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The Court passed the order after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) flagged difficulties in securing prosecution sanctions under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption (PC) Act, including conditional sanctions granted by HDFC Bank. The case concerns tripartite agreements between homebuyers, developers and financial institutions under which builders undertook to pay loan instalments until possession or a stipulated date. However, after the developers defaulted on these payments, financial institutions initiated recovery proceedings against homebuyers, many of whom were yet to receive possession of their properties. In April 2025, the Supreme Court ordered a CBI probe into the alleged nexus between developers and financial institutions. In its sixth supplementary status report, the CBI today informed the Court that investigation has been completed in 25 of the 55 registered cases. While 22 chargesheets have been filed, closure reports have been submitted in three cases, it added. items.title: IRCTC scam: Delhi High Court rejects plea by Lalu Yadav, Rabri Devi, Tejashwi Yadav against trial court order framing charges
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday rejected the petitions filed by former Bihar Chief Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav, his wife Rabri Devi and son Tejashwi Yadav against a trial court order framing criminal charges against them in the alleged IRCTC scam case Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma passed the order. The Court held that the material collected by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) raised grave suspicion of a criminal conspiracy involving manipulation of railway hotel tenders and subsequent transfer of valuable land to Lalu Yadav's family. It said that the material raised grave suspicion that Lalu Yadav, while serving as Railway Minister, abused his position by influencing the process leading to the award of hotel tenders in favour of Sujata Hotel. Justice Sharma noted that the subsequent transfer of the Patna land to his family, through share transactions, could constitute the other side of the alleged quid pro quo arrangement. According to the allegations, during Yadav's tenure as Railway Minister from 2004 to 2009, two IRCTC hotels in Ranchi and Puri were leased to a company named Sujata Hotels through a manipulated tender process. In return, land worth crores was transferred to a company allegedly linked to Lalu’s wife Rabri Devi and son Tejashwi Yadav at a fraction of its market value. items.title: Justice DY Chandrachud-led mediation between Rani Kapur and Priya Kapur fails; Supreme Court to decide on merits
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday closed mediation proceedings between Rani Kapur and her daughter-in-law Priya Sachdev Kapur after efforts to resolve the dispute over late industrialist Sunjay Kapur's family trust failed. Justice Abhay Ahuja Tata Trusts has challenged the September 17 board resolution which reappointed N Chandrasekaran as the executive chairman of Tata Sons and Tata Group. items.title: Supreme Court asks Centre to consider setting up multiple Adjudicating Authorities under PMLA
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday urged the Central government to consider setting up multiple adjudicating authorities to decide whether provisional property attachments by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) should be confirmed. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of the rising number of complaints and applications filed before the adjudicating authority. It added that the increasing caseload, coupled with the time-bound nature of adjudication, puts enormous pressure on the members of the adjudicating authority. The Bench noted that before the 2009 amendment, the PMLA provided for setting up more than one adjudicating authority. It said the Centre could consider restoring that original framework. items.title: Warning labels on packaged food should disclose total sugar, fat; not just added sugar, fat: Supreme Court
items.summary: In a detailed judgment governing packaged food in India and measures to mitigate their health impact, the Supreme Court on Thursday passed a slew of directions to ensure proper disclosure of sugar, salt and saturated fat in such packaged food products. A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran issued detailed directions towards that end with respect to Front-of-Pack Nutrition Labelling (FOPNL) on packaged food products containing high levels of sugar, salt and saturated fat. In this regard, the Court directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to ensure that FOPNL discloses total sugars and saturated fat rather than added sugar and added fat alone as nutrients of concern. "The FSSAI shall ensure that the FOPNL treats total sugars and saturated fat rather than added sugar and added fat as the nutrients of concern alongside salt in alignment with its own long-standing consensus existing prior to the DGI 2024," the Court directed. The thresholds level for sugar and fat should be revisited and calculated based on total value and not with reference to added sugar or fat and the values provided in Dietary Guidelines for India (DGI) 2024 should not be adopted, the Court further said. Thresholds should not be set too low or too high, the bench added. Pertinently, the Court directed that FSSAI shall ensure that each hexagon in the FOPNL carries a standardised pictorial representation of the nutrient of concern together with the corresponding words 'high fat, high sugar or high salt', as the case may be. "The authority shall ensure that the FOPNL provides for a separate hexagon for each nutrient of concern. items.title: Delhi High Court to examine whether AI can be recognised as author under Copyright Act
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday issued notice on an appeal challenging an order of the Copyright Office holding that an artificial intelligence (AI) system cannot be recognised as an author under the Copyright Act, 1957. [Stephen Thaler v. Registrar of Copyrights] Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav sought a response to the appeal filed by American computer scientist Stephen L Thaler and listed the matter for further hearing in March 2027. Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav The appeal concerns the rejection of Thaler's application for registration of copyright in an artwork titled A Recent Entrance to Paradise . The application named his AI system, the Device for the Autonomous Bootstrapping of Unified Sentience (DABUS), as the author and Thaler as the copyright owner. In August 2026, the Copyright Office held that while AI-generated works could satisfy the originality requirement under copyright law, an AI system could not be recognised as their author. “DABUS is not a natural or juristic person recognised in law and cannot be entered as author under Section 2(d)(vi),” Registrar of Copyrights Dr. Unnat P Pandit had held. Section 2(d)(vi) of the Copyright Act defines the author of a computer-generated literary, dramatic, musical or artistic work as “the person who causes the work to be created”. Thaler had argued before the Copyright Office that DABUS autonomously generated the artwork after being trained using photographs taken by him, curated thesaurus entries and English sentences. He claimed that DABUS autonomously generated the artwork without real-time human intervention. The Copyright Office, however, held that Thaler was the person who caused the artwork to be created since he designed the system and determined its training methodology and inputs. While accepting that the artwork satisfied the originality requirement under Section 13 of the Copyright Act, the Registrar held that DABUS lacked the legal personality necessary to claim authorship, own copyright or assign it to Thaler. The application was ultimately rejected after Thaler declined to unconditionally amend the authorship particulars, though the Registrar left open remedies based on corrected particulars. Thaler was represented by advocates Ankit Sahni, Chirag Ahluwalia, Aman Sinha and Goldie Dhama. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday ruled that the adjudicating authority confirming the provisional attachment of properties by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) must include a judicial member. items.title: Constitution Day 2026: The moral heartbeat of the Republic
items.summary: "Constitution is not a mere lawyers' document; it is a vehicle of Life and its spirit is always the spirit of Age." — Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar. As India celebrates Constitution Day, I look back on the deliberations of our founding fathers, who crafted a foundational charter suited for our democratic nation. What I cherish most are its guaranteed fundamental rights, an independent judiciary, checks and balances among the executive, legislature and judiciary, and an independent Election Commission. As Dr Ambedkar reminded the Assembly on November 25, 1949, if things go wrong under a Constitution, the fault lies not with the text, but with those who work it. While volumes can be written about this living document which secures justice, liberty, equality and promotes fraternity, I confine myself here to a single provision that I regard as the moral heartbeat of our Constitution: Article 21. Terse in its language, yet infinite in its interpretive potential, it states: "No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law." Over nearly eight decades, the Supreme Court of India has transformed this narrow procedural safeguard into the bedrock of a substantive rights regime, reflecting a civilisational shift in the relationship between the State and the individual. Debated as Draft Article 15 in the Constituent Assembly, where the Drafting Committee drew upon American constitutional debates and Constitutional Adviser BN Rau's consultations with US Supreme Court Justice Felix Frankfurter alongside global constitutional models, Article 21 was born as a promise. Over time, the judiciary has breathed life into the idea that liberty means far more than the absence of chains; it encompasses dignity, privacy, livelihood, shelter, health and the right to die with grace. Essence and universal scope of Article 21 At its core, Article 21 is rooted in natural rights and human dignity. Mindful of colonial tyranny, the framers affirmed that the State exists to serve, rather than subjugate, its citizens. Article 21 carries a dual character: a negative restraint condemning arbitrary State power and a positive mandate requiring the State to proactively secure conditions for a dignified life. items.title: Bengaluru court grants anticipatory bail to US-based writer, journalist over remarks about Basavanna
items.summary: A Bengaluru court on Wednesday granted anticipatory bail to US-based writer Ravi Hanjagimutt and journalist Vishweshwar Bhat in a criminal case over alleged derogatory remarks about 12th-century social reformer Basavanna and his vachanas (writings) in the book Basava Mantapa . Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge Mohan Prabhu allowed the anticipatory bail pleas filed by the two accused in connection with a case registered against them by the High Grounds police station in Bengaluru. Justice HP Sandesh While denying the relief to the doctor, the Court noted that forensic examination of material sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) confirmed that the signatures belonged to him. It added that though the accused was a gazetted officer competent to attest documents, he had attested residential proof documents for 14 foreign nationals without any supporting documentary proof. “If it was in respect of one or two persons, then this Court would have accepted the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioner. items.title: UK court grants bail to Indian lawyer Vijay Aggarwal on £500,000 bond in sexual assault case
items.summary: A court in the United Kingdom on Wednesday granted bail to prominent Indian criminal lawyer Vijay Aggarwal in a case involving allegations of rape and sexual assault. Judge David Tomlinson of the Southwark Crown Court also granted bail to Aggarwal's assistant Manpreet Kaur, who is a co-accused in the case. Aggarwal was directed to furnish a bond of £500,000 while Kaur was directed to furnish a bond of £200,000. Both have been barred from travelling outside the United Kingdom. Aggarwal and Kaur were present in court during the hearing. Aggarwal's wife, daughter and son-in-law were also present. Aggarwal and Kaur were arrested by the Metropolitan Police on August 11 from a property in London's Mayfair area . The arrests followed complaints of sexual assault in connection with incidents alleged to have occurred on May 26 and August 9 this year. Aggarwal currently faces one charge of rape and three charges of sexual assault. Southwark Crown Court had earlier rejected Aggarwal's bail application on September 23 on the ground that he posed a flight risk. During the latest bail hearing, the Court was informed that British authorities had contacted around 2,000 women and interviewed around 500 of them as part of the investigation. Aggarwal's lawyer submitted that the sexual intercourse which formed the basis of the rape allegation was consensual. The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) opposed the bail applications, citing the risk of the accused absconding. However, the Court agreed to release both accused on stringent bail conditions. Aggarwal will also be subjected to electronic monitoring. The trial is scheduled to commence on March 15, 2027 and is expected to last four weeks. Aggarwal is a prominent Delhi-based criminal lawyer who has represented several high-profile clients in white-collar crime cases, including businessmen Mehul Choksi and Nirav Modi and former ICICI Bank CEO Chanda Kochhar. items.title: Tiger Shroff firing: Mumbai court finds one of the accused to be minor, transfers him to Juvenile Board
items.summary: A special court under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOC Act) in Mumbai on Wednesday ordered the transfer of one of the accused in the Tiger Shroff firing incident to the Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) after an inquiry confirmed that he was a minor on the date of the offence [Child in Conflict of Law v. State of Maharashtra]. Special judge Satyanarayan R Navander passed the order on an application moved by the father of the child who claimed that his son was a minor. Eleven persons, including two women, are accused in the case in which six rounds of gun shots were fired at Shroff’s vehicle on the evening of October 18 as he was exiting a football ground in Juhu. While the actor escaped unhurt, his driver and a bystander sustained bullet injuries. The Mumbai Police subsequently registered an FIR for attempt to murder alongside offences punishable under the Arms Act and later invoked the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act, 1999 (MCOCA). The investigation has pointed to transnational coordination linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi syndicate. The special court had earlier remanded the 11 accused to police custody. The father of one of the accused then moved the Court seeking an age determination inquiry. He contended that his son was born on November 30, 2008, and had not completed 18 years of age when the incident occurred on October 18. After the court’s directions, the investigating officer verified the educational and civic records of the accused and submitted a report. Documentary evidence gathered during the inquiry included the School Leaving Certificate, Certificate of Secondary Examination, school admission and withdrawal register and the official birth certificate. All records corroborated the date of birth claimed by the father. The prosecution submitted before the Court that a suitable order may be passed in view of the verification report. “ From the inquiry conducted by this court under Section 9 of the Juvenile Justice Act, the accused is found to be a ‘child’ on the date of the incident. Therefore, it is necessary to produce him before the Juvenile Justice Board. Further adjudication of the offence so far as the accused is concerned, it be held before the JJB," the Court said. Accordingly, the Court directed Taloja Central Prison authorities to hand over the child to the investigating officer for immediate production before the Juvenile Justice Board in Mumbai. items.title: Delhi High Court issues summons in  Abhishek Sharma's personality rights suit, directs removal of offending content
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday sought responses of individuals and entities accused of violating Indian cricketer Abhishek Sharma's personality rights by publishing allegedly defamatory, obscene and AI-generated content about him. .Justice Jyoti Singh said the Court will direct the removal of certain offending online content against Sharma. "At this point in time, I will direct their takedown and I will injunct the defendants as we usually do," said the Court. Justice Jyoti Singh Additionally, the Court directed issuance of summons and notice to the defendants through their social media handles and addresses. The matter has been listed for further hearing on November 17. Sharma moved the Court seeking protection of his personality rights and takedown of alleged defamatory and Artificial Intelligence-generated (AI) content portraying him in bad light. Sharma in the suit sought takedown of certain infringing content including AI-generated material circulating on social media. He alleged that several social media posts use AI-generated images and misleading captions to portray him falsely. During the previous hearing , his counsel had argued that one such AI-generated post falsely depicted Sharma with his manager and referred to her as his girlfriend, thereby creating a misleading impression. During today's hearing, advocate Bahl, appearing for Sharma, informed the Court that pursuant to the additional affidavit filed in compliance with its earlier order, several of the offending URLs had already been taken down. Appearing for Meta Platforms, advocate Varun Pathak submitted that only two offending URLs remained on Meta's platforms and assured the Court that those Instagram links would also be removed. The Court thereafter examined the Facebook and Instagram posts placed on record and scrutinised the list of URLs flagged in the plaint. Bahl further submitted that some of the remaining material was obscene and profane. He also pointed out that unauthorised listings using Sharma's identity continued to be available on e-commerce platforms, including Amazon and Flipkart. Advocates Gaurav Bahl, Anku Khanna, Arundhati Dhar, Harshita and Sachin Thakker appeared for Sharma. items.title: Thiruparankundram and Hindutva | The men claiming to know what's best for women | South Central 103
items.summary: What happens when a centuries-old religious dispute becomes a political flashpoint? How has the controversy over lighting a lamp atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai been used to fuel communal tensions in Tamil Nadu? The discussion traces the dispute back to the 19th century, exploring its history, the hill's significance to Hindus, Muslims and Jains, and how successive governments have handled the conflict. The conversation looks at a Tamil Nadu government archaeological survey that identified the disputed pillar as a British-era triangulation marker, rather than a lamp pillar. Sudipto discusses how the dispute has evolved over more than a century, the role of successive governments and the ways in which Hindutva politics has attempted to turn a shared religious space into a site of communal mobilisation. The discussion also examines the role of the judiciary, the growing polarisation around the issue and how social media and political groups are shaping the narrative. In the second part of the episode, the hosts are joined by The News Minute's Lakshmi Priya to discuss her investigation, ‘Unmasking Misogyny: How a Malayalam YouTube channel weaponised science against women’. items.title: Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh arrested for allegedly sexually harassing IAS officer
items.summary: After four days of public outcry and strong opposition from political parties, the Tamil Nadu police arrested Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA C Arul Vignesh on November 27 for allegedly sexually harassing a woman IAS officer. A police team led by Investigating officer Shristi Singh arrested the MLA from his residence. Before the arrest, the MLA’s residence was cordoned off and a large number of police were deployed to take him into custody. A First Information Report (FIR) was registered against him at the All Women Police Station (AWPS) in Kallakurichi on November 24. The MLA has been booked under sections 75 (sexual harassment), 78(2) (stalking) and 132 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their duty) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Section 4 of Prevention of Sexual Harassment (PoSH) Act. The case was registered after the woman IAS officer submitted a written complaint to Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary M Sai Kumar on November 23 under the PoSH Act. The arrest came shortly after the Supreme Court slammed the state government for defying its order to light the lamp at the disputed Deepathoon, atop the Thiruparankundram hill. The case was registered against the Kallakurichi legislator following the intervention of the Madras High Court. While the state initially maintained that neither the police nor the Chief Secretary had received a formal complaint. It changed its stand during the hearing on November 24, when State Public Prosecutor R John Sathyan told the court that the IAS officer had submitted a complaint and that an FIR had been registered at the AWPS in Kallakurichi.

items.title: SC orders lamp to be lit at Thiruparankundram Deepathoon on Nov 28, suspends temple trustees
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday suspended the board of trustees of the Thiruparankundram temple in Madurai district and ordered that the Karthigai Deepam be lit at the disputed pillar or Deepathoon on Saturday, November 28, after its earlier order was not carried out. A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi appointed former High Court judges Justice S Vaidyanathan and Justice V Parthipan as receivers to administer the temple, according to the Live Law. They have to ensure that the lamp is lit, using the flame at Uchipillaiyar. The Supreme Court has also handed over the security of the entire hill to the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), citing the failure of the Tamil Nadu Police to implement its orders. The court has directed CRPF to ensure the peaceful functioning of the temple and the Dargah. A Siva temple and the Uchi Pillaiyar temple are located on the lower part of the Tirupurakundram hill, while the dargah stands at its summit. For decades, the customary Karthigai Deepam has been lit near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple by the temple management. In 2025, however, Hindutva groups went to court demanding that the lamp be lit on the ‘deepathoon’, a stone pillar located at the hilltop, about 50 metres from the dargah. The DMK government did not implement the court’s order, and the new TVK government has followed the same course, this time citing the temple Devasthanam’s decision. The Supreme Court strongly criticised the Tamil Nadu government for not lighting the Karthigai Deepam at the pillar on November 24, as said in its earlier order.
